prompts.title: Space Shooter
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js space shooter game. The player controls a spaceship that can move in all directions and shoot projectiles at incoming enemy waves. Include particle effects for explosions, a starfield background, score display, health bar, and progressive difficulty. Enemies should have different movement patterns and the game should have a game-over screen with restart.
prompts.notes: Watch for: no collision detection; enemies don't vary; no game-over state; poor performance with many particles.

prompts.title: Tower Defense
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js tower defense game on a grid-based map. Players place different tower types along a path to stop waves of enemies from reaching the base. Include tower upgrade mechanics, enemy health bars, a currency system, wave counter, and speed controls. Towers should have visible attack ranges and projectile animations.
prompts.notes: Watch for: enemies ignore path; towers don't target correctly; no economy balance; performance drops with many enemies.

prompts.title: Cloth Physics Simulator
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js cloth simulation using a spring-mass model. Render a rectangular cloth mesh pinned at the top corners that responds to gravity and wind. The user can drag cloth vertices with the mouse, adjust wind direction/strength with sliders, and toggle pins on/off. Include self-collision detection and a wireframe toggle.
prompts.notes: Watch for: cloth stretches infinitely; no self-collision; simulation unstable at high wind; mouse drag doesn't raycast correctly.

prompts.title: Solar System Orrery
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page Three.js solar system simulation with accurate relative planet sizes and orbital periods. Include all 8 planets with orbits shown as elliptical lines, a time speed control, planet labels that face the camera, click-to-focus on any planet with smooth camera transition, and an info panel showing the selected planet's data. Add a toggleable asteroid belt and moon orbits for Earth and Jupiter.
prompts.notes: Watch for: planets overlap due to scale; orbits not elliptical; camera transition jarring; labels unreadable at distance.

prompts.title: Voxel Sculpting Tool
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js voxel sculpting tool with brush size controls, multiple materials (at least 6 colors), undo/redo with Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y, and JSON export of the voxel data. Include a material palette, brush size slider (1-5 voxels), eraser mode, grid visualization toggle, and camera orbit controls. The tool should support click-to-place and click-drag-to-paint workflows.
prompts.notes: Watch for: missing undo; slow updates with many voxels; weak raycasting on faces; paint bleeds to wrong face.

prompts.title: Terrain Painter
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page Three.js terrain editor with height painting. Start with a flat grid plane that the user can sculpt by painting height values. Include raise/lower/smooth/flatten brush modes, adjustable brush size and strength, texture layers (grass, rock, snow) painted by altitude, water level slider, and a minimap showing the terrain from above. Export the heightmap as an image.
prompts.notes: Watch for: normals not updated after edit; brush doesn't follow terrain surface; smooth mode doesn't work; performance with large grid.

prompts.title: Fractal Explorer
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js 3D fractal explorer. Render a Mandelbulb or Menger sponge using raymarching in a fragment shader displayed on a full-screen quad. Include zoom controls, iteration depth slider, color palette selection (at least 4 palettes), orbit camera, cross-section plane that slices through the fractal, and a screenshot button. Show render time per frame.
prompts.notes: Watch for: shader compilation errors; raymarching artifacts at edges; too slow without adaptive stepping; cross-section doesn't work.

prompts.title: Underwater Exploration
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js underwater exploration scene. The player swims through a coral reef environment using WASD + mouse look. Include procedurally generated coral formations, schools of fish using boid behavior, caustic light patterns on the sea floor, floating particle effects (bubbles, plankton), depth-based fog that increases with depth, and an oxygen meter that depletes over time. Find hidden treasure items scattered in the reef.
prompts.notes: Watch for: fish swim through coral; no sense of being underwater; caustics look wrong; oxygen timer feels arbitrary.

prompts.title: Neon City Flythrough
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page Three.js scene of a synthwave neon city made from procedural box buildings. Include animated camera flythrough, emissive windows, atmospheric fog, and a starfield background. Add keyboard controls (WASD + mouse look), and expose fly speed, fog density, and building density in a small on-screen control panel. Output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: controls fighting the automated camera; repetitive buildings; excessive bloom or fog hiding the scene; pointer lock not explained or released cleanly.

prompts.title: Procedural Terrain Biomes
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page Three.js terrain generator using layered noise. Include mountains, plains, and valleys with color-by-height biome shading, directional sunlight, soft shadows, and orbit controls. Add a smooth day/night cycle that changes sky and fog color. Provide sliders for noise scale, octave count, and water level. Output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: controls that do not regenerate terrain; abrupt biome bands; mismatched water and terrain levels; expensive geometry rebuilds on every slider event.

prompts.title: Audio-Reactive Crystal Field
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page Three.js experience with hundreds of crystal spikes that react to audio frequency bands from the Web Audio API. Animate scale, hue, and emissive intensity from bass/mid/treble ranges. Include fallback demo animation if mic permission is denied. Keep frame rate smooth and output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: no user-gesture audio unlock; all crystals reacting identically; missing microphone-denied fallback; excessive material or draw-call overhead.

prompts.title: Exploding Modular Cube
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js demo of a segmented cube that explodes outward on click and reassembles with easing. Add raycast hover highlighting, piece spin animation, and user controls for explosion strength and reset. Keep visuals clean with shadows and soft ambient fill. Output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: pieces reassembling in the wrong orientation; hover state sticking; explosion direction not based on each piece position; animation state breaking on repeated clicks.

prompts.title: GPU Galaxy Particles
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page Three.js particle galaxy with at least 200k points using BufferGeometry. Add spiral arms, color gradients from core to rim, subtle rotation, and mouse parallax camera movement. Include a small HUD showing particle count and FPS. Output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: constructing one object per particle; inaccurate FPS or particle HUD values; flat random-disc distribution instead of spiral arms; unnecessary per-frame buffer uploads.

prompts.title: Portal Chamber
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page Three.js sci-fi chamber with a central portal ring and animated portal surface distortion. Use shader material effects (or UV distortion) for swirling energy, emissive rim lighting, drifting dust particles, and a slow cinematic camera. Output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: a static portal texture; blown-out emissive materials; transparent effects sorting incorrectly; camera framing that clips the chamber.

prompts.title: Jelly Cube
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js soft-body illusion: a cube mesh with vertex wobble, spring damping, and mouse-proximity deformation. Add a reflective floor, balanced PBR lighting, and a toggle between wireframe and shaded mode. Output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: cumulative vertex drift; deformation calculated in the wrong coordinate space; unstable spring motion; reflections overwhelming the object.

prompts.title: Rainy Cyber Alley
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page Three.js rainy cyberpunk alley with falling rain particles, animated neon signs, puddle reflections, and drifting steam quads. Add occasional lightning flashes that momentarily increase scene exposure. Include orbit + slight walk controls. Output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: rain passing visibly through roofs; fake reflections that do not align with the scene; transparent steam artifacts; walk and orbit controls conflicting.

prompts.title: Mini Planet
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js low-poly tiny planet scene with procedural placement of trees, houses, and rocks on a sphere. Include rotating clouds, toon-style shading, and click-to-focus camera transitions. Keep assets fully procedural (no external models). Output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: props not aligned to the sphere normal; overlapping placements; click targets too small; camera transitions passing through the planet.

prompts.title: Fractal Tunnel
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page Three.js abstract fractal tunnel ride with repeated geometric segments, color pulses, and forward camera travel. Add controls for speed, palette, and pulse frequency. Ensure the animation loops smoothly. Output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: visible popping at the loop boundary; camera clipping through segments; flickering high-frequency colour pulses; unbounded geometry growth.

prompts.title: Magnetic Marbles
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js marble playground with simplified physics (velocity + damping + collisions). Let users place attractor/repulsor points by clicking. Render motion trails and add reset/randomize controls. Output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: singular forces launching marbles at close range; unstable collision resolution; trails causing unbounded allocations; unclear attractor versus repulsor feedback.

prompts.title: Hologram Showcase
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page Three.js product pedestal viewer with a floating object, hologram scanline effect, rim lights, and hotspot labels. Add smooth click-to-focus transitions and auto-rotation toggle. Keep layout minimal and cinematic. Output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: hotspot labels drifting from their anchors; scanlines ignoring object depth; auto-rotation fighting focus transitions; poor text contrast.

prompts.title: Voxel Builder
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js voxel editor where users place/remove blocks with raycasting and grid snapping. Include color picker, ghost preview cube, save/load from localStorage, and clear scene button. Output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: placing blocks inside occupied cells; removing the wrong face; ghost preview not matching grid placement; malformed localStorage data breaking startup.

prompts.title: Lava Planet
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page Three.js lava planet with animated emissive cracks, atmosphere shell glow, and orbiting debris. Add configurable rotation speed and glow intensity. Keep materials dramatic and high contrast. Output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: cracks that rotate independently of the surface; atmosphere rendered as an opaque shell; excessive glow losing surface detail; debris intersecting the planet.

prompts.title: Endless Runner Prototype
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js endless runner prototype with procedural track chunks, moving obstacles, score counter, and collision detection. Add jump/slide keyboard actions and restart flow. Keep it compact but polished. Output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: gaps between recycled track chunks; frame-rate-dependent movement; unreliable jump or slide hitboxes; restart leaving stale obstacles or timers.

prompts.title: DNA Sculpture
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page Three.js animated DNA helix made from spheres and connecting cylinders, with gradient color mapping and gentle camera orbit. Add controls for helix pitch, radius, and rotation speed. Output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: connector cylinders not oriented between bases; control changes rebuilding excessive geometry; incorrect paired-strand phase; motion that causes nausea.

prompts.title: Origami Fold
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js origami-inspired folding animation transforming a flat mesh into a complex abstract shape over time. Provide a timeline scrubber and play/pause controls. Include wireframe overlay option. Output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: linear vertex morphing that does not resemble folding; timeline and playback falling out of sync; self-intersecting faces; wireframe z-fighting.

prompts.title: Storm Ocean
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page Three.js storm ocean scene with wave displacement, moody sky dome, and random lightning flashes affecting global lighting. Add camera drift and wind intensity controls. Output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: waves moving without updated normals; lightning that only changes the background; horizon seams; camera clipping below the water surface.

prompts.title: Sci-Fi Hangar Drones
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js sci-fi hangar with hovering drones, animated warning lights, emissive runway strips, and subtle volumetric-style fog planes. Include drone formation toggle and cinematic camera path. Output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: drones clipping into one another during formation changes; fog planes visibly intersecting geometry; warning lights not affecting nearby surfaces; camera leaving the hangar.

prompts.title: 3D Ribbon Painter
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page Three.js interactive ribbon painter where mouse movement generates 3D ribbon trails with additive blending and fade-out. Add color picker, trail width control, clear button, and screenshot button. Output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: ribbons twisting or collapsing at sharp turns; unbounded geometry growth; fade-out only changing material opacity globally; screenshots omitting the WebGL canvas.

prompts.title: 3D Gravity Well Simulation
prompts.prompt: Create an interactive 3D simulation of a gravity well using Three.js, HTML, and CSS. The simulation should feature a deformable 3D grid representing spacetime. Allow the user to place multiple massive objects (e.g., stars, black holes) at arbitrary locations on the grid. Each massive object should visually deform the grid based on its mass, demonstrating spacetime curvature. Implement the ability to launch small particles with adjustable initial velocities. Display the trajectories of these particles as they move through the warped spacetime, bending realistically around the massive objects. Include controls to adjust the mass and initial velocity of objects and particles. The visual style should be clean and intuitive, clearly illustrating the effect of gravity on the fabric of spacetime. Ensure the application is a single HTML page with embedded CSS and JavaScript (Three.js).
prompts.notes: Watch for: grid deformation presented as the particle physics itself; unstable integration near massive objects; trajectories growing without bounds; controls not applying to the selected object or particle.

prompts.title: GTA 6 Game
prompts.prompt: Build a polished single-page Three.js open-world crime-action game inspired by GTA 6, set in an original neon coastal city. Deliver one standalone HTML file with embedded CSS and JavaScript; Three.js may be loaded from a public CDN, but do not use copyrighted logos, named characters, map data, audio, or ripped assets. Create all visuals from performant low-poly procedural geometry and simple generated textures. The game must be immediately playable and include: a third-person character with responsive WASD movement, sprint, jump, mouse-controlled camera, basic raycast shooting, health, and the ability to enter or exit nearby vehicles with E; arcade vehicle handling with acceleration, braking, reverse, steering, collisions, vehicle durability, and a smooth chase camera; a compact explorable city containing roads and intersections, varied buildings, a beach and ocean, palm trees, neon nightlife areas, ramps, streetlights, and recognizable landmarks; ambient traffic following road routes and pedestrians wandering on pavements with lightweight avoidance behavior; and a mission loop with clear objectives such as reaching a contact, stealing a marked car, collecting packages, escaping a pursuit, and delivering the vehicle to a safehouse for a cash reward. Add a 0-to-5-star wanted system: reckless driving, attacking civilians, or shooting raises the level; police cars spawn at sensible road positions, pursue the player, and search nearby after losing sight; the wanted level falls only after the player evades police for a visible cooldown. Include a polished HUD with health, vehicle durability, cash, wanted stars, current mission text, contextual control prompts, and a rotating minimap showing roads, the player, mission waypoint, police, and nearby vehicles. Add a warm sunset-to-night lighting cycle with neon signs becoming brighter after dark, shadows, atmospheric fog, subtle ocean animation, tyre smoke, collision sparks, muzzle flashes, and restrained screen shake. Provide a title/start overlay, concise controls guide, pause support, game-over and mission-complete states, and a restart button. Use delta-time movement, object pooling for transient effects, capped NPC counts, simple collision volumes, and distance-based updates so the game remains smooth. Avoid placeholder buttons, TODOs, or purely decorative systems: every displayed control and gameplay feature must work.
prompts.notes: Watch for: a static city with no real gameplay loop; entering vehicles that breaks player or camera state; frame-rate-dependent driving; traffic and police ignoring roads; wanted stars that never decay; missions that cannot complete; minimap markers using the wrong orientation; excessive meshes, shadows, or NPC updates causing poor performance.

prompts.title: Flow Field Painter
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page p5.js sketch: a Perlin-noise flow field painter. Thousands of particles follow the field and leave fading translucent trails that build up into a painting. Include sliders for noise scale, particle count, and trail opacity, a colour palette selector with at least 4 curated palettes, click-to-reseed with a new field, and a button to save the canvas as a PNG. The result should stay smooth at 60fps with at least 2000 particles.
prompts.notes: Watch for: trails erased every frame instead of accumulating; particles cluster at edges; frame rate collapse at high counts; palettes look muddy.

prompts.title: Falling Sand Automaton
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page p5.js falling-sand cellular automaton. Implement at least five elements with distinct behaviours: sand (falls and piles), water (flows sideways), stone (static), fire (rises, burns wood and dies out), and wood (flammable, static). Provide an element picker, adjustable brush size, an eraser, pause/step controls, and a clear button. The grid should be at least 200x150 cells and update smoothly.
prompts.notes: Watch for: sand falls through water unrealistically; water never levels out; fire spreads instantly or never; update order artifacts (left-to-right bias).

prompts.title: Audio-Reactive Visualizer
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page p5.js audio-reactive visualizer using microphone input. Show a circular FFT spectrum, a waveform ring, and a particle system that pulses on detected beats. Include a sensitivity slider, at least 3 visual themes, and a smooth idle animation plus a clear message when microphone access is denied or unavailable. Audio must only start after a user gesture (click to start).
prompts.notes: Watch for: no user-gesture audio unlock; crash when mic denied; beat detection that just maps volume; visuals not actually driven by FFT bands.

prompts.title: Boids Flocking Playground
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page p5.js boids flocking simulation with at least 200 boids at 60fps. Provide live sliders for separation, alignment, and cohesion weights plus perception radius. Holding the mouse button spawns a predator at the cursor that the flock flees from. Include wrap-around edges, a toggle to visualize one boid's perception radius and neighbours, and a boid count slider.
prompts.notes: Watch for: O(n^2) neighbour search killing the frame rate; boids jitter instead of flocking; sliders that don't visibly change behaviour; predator ignored.

prompts.title: Recursive Seasonal Tree
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page p5.js sketch of a recursive fractal tree that cycles through the four seasons: spring buds, lush summer leaves, autumn colours with falling leaves, and a bare winter tree with falling snow. Branches should sway gently in the wind. Include sliders for branch angle and recursion depth, a season speed control, and click-to-regrow a new randomized tree. Render at least 8 levels of recursion smoothly.
prompts.notes: Watch for: tree redrawn identically every frame (no randomness persistence); falling leaves not tied to the tree; recursion depth slider causing freezes; wind sway rotating the whole tree rigidly.

prompts.title: Kaleidoscope Drawing App
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page p5.js kaleidoscope drawing app. Strokes drawn with the mouse are mirrored across an adjustable number of symmetry segments (4 to 16, with optional reflection within each segment). Include a brush size slider, a colour mode that slowly cycles hue while drawing, an undo button for the last stroke, clear, and save-as-PNG. Show a subtle guide overlay of the symmetry segments that can be toggled off.
prompts.notes: Watch for: mirroring math wrong off-centre; undo clears everything; hue cycling resets every stroke; guide lines baked into the saved PNG.

prompts.title: Double Pendulum Chaos
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page p5.js double pendulum simulation using the real equations of motion (not faked). Show three pendulums started with infinitesimally different initial angles in different colours to demonstrate chaotic divergence, each leaving a fading trail. Allow dragging either bob to set new initial conditions (which resets all three), a trail length slider, a gravity slider, and a readout of total energy to show the integration is stable.
prompts.notes: Watch for: energy blowing up (bad integrator); pendulums not actually diverging (same seeds); drag interaction fighting the physics; trails drawn as connected lines across resets.

prompts.title: Metaball Lava Lamp
prompts.prompt: Create a single-page p5.js lava lamp using metaballs. Blobs rise and fall with heat-driven buoyancy, merge and split visually using a proper field-threshold technique (marching squares or per-pixel field evaluation — not just overlapping circles). The mouse gently attracts nearby blobs. Include a blob count slider, at least 4 colour themes with smooth gradients, and a glass-lamp silhouette frame around the simulation.
prompts.notes: Watch for: blobs are plain circles that overlap without merging; per-pixel evaluation too slow at full resolution; blobs escaping the lamp; buoyancy looks like random drift.

prompts.title: Wordle Clone
prompts.prompt: Build a complete Wordle clone as a single HTML page using only vanilla JavaScript and CSS — no libraries. Embed a word list of at least 300 common 5-letter words. Include the 6-guess grid with flip animations, an on-screen keyboard that mirrors letter states (correct/present/absent), physical keyboard support, invalid-word shake feedback, a share button that copies the emoji result grid, and win/loss statistics persisted in localStorage.
prompts.notes: Watch for: duplicate-letter colouring wrong (the classic bug); word list too small or invalid words accepted; keyboard state not updating; stats not persisting.

prompts.title: Canvas Asteroids
prompts.prompt: Build the classic Asteroids game on a single HTML page with vanilla JavaScript and a canvas — no libraries. Vector-line aesthetic, ship with rotation and thrust momentum, screen wrap-around, asteroids that split into smaller pieces when shot, occasional UFO, hyperspace jump on a key press, progressive levels, lives, score, and a localStorage high-score table. Add simple retro sound effects synthesized with the Web Audio API (no audio files).
prompts.notes: Watch for: no momentum/inertia on the ship; collision detection using bounding boxes on rotated shapes; asteroids spawning on top of the player; audio context not unlocked by user gesture.

prompts.title: Pixel Art Editor
prompts.prompt: Build a pixel art editor as a single HTML page in vanilla JavaScript — no libraries. Support 16x16, 32x32, and 64x64 canvases, a default palette plus a custom colour picker, pencil, flood fill, eraser, and eyedropper tools, undo/redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y), a live preview at actual size, grid toggle, save/load named drawings via localStorage, and PNG export at a selectable scale (1x/4x/8x). Drawing should work with click and drag, including outside-the-lines drag handling.
prompts.notes: Watch for: flood fill stack overflow or filling the whole canvas; undo history capturing every drag pixel as a separate step; export ignoring the chosen scale; mouseup outside the canvas leaving the tool stuck down.

prompts.title: WebAudio Synth Keyboard
prompts.prompt: Build a playable synthesizer as a single HTML page using the Web Audio API and vanilla JavaScript — no libraries or audio files. Two octaves of on-screen piano keys playable by mouse/touch and computer keyboard (with the key map shown), waveform selector (sine/square/saw/triangle), ADSR envelope sliders, a low-pass filter cutoff/resonance control, a delay effect with feedback, polyphony, and a real-time oscilloscope display of the output. Audio must start only after a user gesture.
prompts.notes: Watch for: clicks/pops from missing envelope ramps; notes sticking when keys are released outside the element; no polyphony (one oscillator reused); oscilloscope not connected to the actual output chain.

prompts.title: Tetris
prompts.prompt: Build a full-featured Tetris as a single HTML page in vanilla JavaScript — no libraries. Include the 7 standard tetrominoes with correct colours, SRS-style wall kicks, hold piece, next-piece queue showing 3 pieces, ghost piece, soft and hard drop, line-clear animation, levels that speed up, standard scoring (single/double/triple/tetris with level multiplier), pause, game over with restart, and a localStorage high score. Support both keyboard controls and on-screen buttons for touch.
prompts.notes: Watch for: rotation near walls failing (no kicks); hold allowing infinite swaps; gravity tied to frame rate instead of a timer; line clear removing wrong rows.

prompts.title: Typing Speed Test
prompts.prompt: Build a typing speed test as a single HTML page in vanilla JavaScript — no libraries. Show a flowing stream of random common words; typed characters are marked correct/incorrect in place with a caret that advances. Offer 30s and 60s modes, live WPM and accuracy that update while typing, and a results screen with final WPM, accuracy, a per-key error breakdown, and a canvas line graph of WPM over the duration of the test. Store past results in localStorage and chart the history on a separate tab.
prompts.notes: Watch for: WPM computed from characters without the /5 convention; backspace handling corrupting the comparison; timer starting before the first keystroke; results graph axes unlabeled or unscaled.

prompts.title: Markdown Previewer (Own Parser)
prompts.prompt: Build a split-pane markdown previewer as a single HTML page where you must write the markdown parser yourself in vanilla JavaScript — absolutely no libraries. Support headings, bold, italic, inline code, fenced code blocks, links, images, ordered and unordered lists with nesting, blockquotes, horizontal rules, and tables. The preview updates live as you type, scroll position stays roughly synchronized between panes, and the output must be HTML-escaped so script tags in the input cannot execute. Pre-fill the editor with a document demonstrating every supported feature.
prompts.notes: Watch for: nested lists broken; bold/italic regex greediness mangling text; raw HTML injection (XSS) not escaped; code blocks having their contents parsed as markdown.

prompts.title: Kanban Board
prompts.prompt: Build a kanban board as a single HTML page in vanilla JavaScript — no libraries. Columns can be added, renamed, reordered, and deleted; cards support a title, description, coloured labels, and a due date that highlights when overdue. Cards drag and drop between and within columns using native HTML5 drag-and-drop with a clear drop indicator. Everything persists to localStorage, and there are export-to-JSON and import-from-JSON buttons. Include sensible empty states and keyboard access for adding/editing cards.
prompts.notes: Watch for: drop position always appending to the end; dragover not preventing default (drop never fires); state not persisted after every mutation; deleting a column orphaning its cards silently.

prompts.title: Raymarched Mandelbulb
prompts.prompt: Create a single HTML page that renders a raymarched Mandelbulb fractal in a full-screen WebGL fragment shader. Write all the WebGL boilerplate in plain JavaScript — no libraries. Include mouse-drag orbit and scroll zoom, a power slider (2–12) that morphs the fractal, at least 3 colour palettes based on orbit traps or iteration count, soft shadows or ambient occlusion for depth, and an FPS counter. The shader must compile cleanly and degrade gracefully (lower max steps) when slow.
prompts.notes: Watch for: shader compile errors (the #1 failure); banding/overstep artifacts; camera math gimbal-locking; fractal silhouette but no surface detail.

prompts.title: Animated Voronoi Flow
prompts.prompt: Create a single HTML page with a full-screen WebGL fragment shader showing animated Voronoi cells whose seed points drift smoothly over time. Write all WebGL boilerplate in plain JavaScript — no libraries. Cell edges should glow, cell interiors should shade by distance to the seed, and the pattern near the mouse cursor should ripple or distort. Include sliders for cell density and animation speed, and a colour scheme selector with at least 3 schemes.
prompts.notes: Watch for: cell edges aliased/flickering; seeds jumping instead of drifting (no smooth hash animation); mouse uniform in wrong coordinate space; density slider requiring recompile.

prompts.title: Water Caustics Pool
prompts.prompt: Create a single HTML page with a full-screen WebGL fragment shader of looking down into a sunlit swimming pool: a tiled floor with animated caustic light patterns, subtle surface refraction distorting the tiles, and volumetric light shafts. Write all WebGL boilerplate in plain JavaScript — no libraries. Clicking spawns an expanding ripple ring that distorts the caustics, with several simultaneous ripples supported via uniforms. Include a sun-angle slider and a water-depth slider.
prompts.notes: Watch for: caustics that are just scrolling noise; ripples not affecting the refraction; tile pattern without perspective; click coordinates flipped vertically.

prompts.title: Raymarched Clouds
prompts.prompt: Create a single HTML page with a full-screen WebGL fragment shader rendering volumetric clouds over a gradient sky using raymarched FBM noise. Write all WebGL boilerplate in plain JavaScript — no libraries. The clouds should drift slowly, be lit by a sun whose direction follows the mouse position, and show silver-lining scattering when backlit. Include a time-of-day slider that moves the sun from dawn through midday to dusk with appropriate sky colours, and a cloud-coverage slider.
prompts.notes: Watch for: clouds looking like flat noise (no lighting integration along the ray); frame rate collapse from too many octaves/steps; sun direction not matching the visual sun position; banding without dithering.

prompts.title: Procedural Fire
prompts.prompt: Create a single HTML page with a full-screen WebGL fragment shader of a procedural torch flame: noise-driven flame body with a believable hot-core-to-smoke colour ramp (white/yellow core, orange mid, red edges, dark smoke), upward advection, flickering, and drifting spark particles. Write all WebGL boilerplate in plain JavaScript — no libraries. Include a wind slider that bends the flame, an intensity/fuel slider that changes flame height, and a button cycling between torch, campfire, and candle presets.
prompts.notes: Watch for: flame that scrolls uniformly upward like a texture; colour ramp with hard bands; wind translating the whole flame instead of bending it; sparks on a visible grid.

prompts.title: CRT Post-Processing
prompts.prompt: Create a single HTML page that renders a simple animated test scene (bouncing shapes or scrolling text drawn to an offscreen canvas or framebuffer) and then applies a CRT post-processing shader: scanlines, barrel/curvature distortion with darkened corners, RGB phosphor mask, chromatic aberration, slight bloom, occasional horizontal sync wobble, and animated noise/grain. Write all WebGL boilerplate in plain JavaScript — no libraries. Provide individual toggles and strength sliders for each effect and a master 'CRT off' bypass for comparison.
prompts.notes: Watch for: effects applied to a black screen (source scene never rendered into the texture); curvature sampling outside the texture leaving smears; scanlines aliasing with the display resolution; toggles that don't actually isolate effects.

prompts.title: Shader Game of Life
prompts.prompt: Create a single HTML page implementing Conway's Game of Life entirely on the GPU using ping-pong framebuffers and a WebGL fragment shader. Write all WebGL boilerplate in plain JavaScript — no libraries. The grid should be at least 512x512. Drawing with the mouse paints live cells (with adjustable brush size), and cells are coloured by age (newborn bright, old cells fading through a palette). Include play/pause, single-step, speed control, randomize, clear, and a couple of classic pattern stamps (glider gun, pulsar) placeable at the cursor.
prompts.notes: Watch for: reading and writing the same texture (no ping-pong, corrupt state); neighbour sampling off by half a texel; mouse painting in the wrong place due to coordinate flip; age colouring lost because state is binary.

prompts.title: Ocean Seascape
prompts.prompt: Create a single HTML page with a full-screen WebGL fragment shader rendering an open ocean: layered FBM or Gerstner-style waves with proper normals, sun glint and specular reflection, sky reflection that varies with viewing angle (fresnel), foam on wave crests, and atmospheric haze toward the horizon. Write all WebGL boilerplate in plain JavaScript — no libraries. Mouse Y controls camera height from just above the surface to a high vantage, and a storm slider morphs the sea from calm glass to heavy swell with matching sky.
prompts.notes: Watch for: waves that are just scrolling bump noise with no horizon; missing fresnel so water looks like plastic; foam painted everywhere; horizon line curving or breaking at screen edges.

prompts.title: Flappy Bird Clone
prompts.prompt: Build a Flappy Bird clone as a single HTML page with vanilla JavaScript and canvas — no libraries or image assets; draw the bird, pipes, ground, and parallax background in code. Include tap/click/spacebar flapping with believable gravity and rotation, randomized pipe gaps, score with medal tiers on the game-over screen, a localStorage best score, day/night alternating backgrounds, and a subtle screen shake on death. The game must be restartable instantly.
prompts.notes: Watch for: physics tied to frame rate; hitboxes much larger than the drawn bird; pipes spawning unwinnable gaps; no idle/ready state before the first flap.

prompts.title: Verlet Ragdoll Playground
prompts.prompt: Build a 2D ragdoll physics playground as a single HTML page using verlet integration in vanilla JavaScript and canvas — no physics libraries. A humanoid ragdoll made of particles and distance constraints (with joint angle limits so limbs don't fold backwards) can be grabbed and thrown with the mouse. Include static obstacles (ramps, pegs, a seesaw), a gravity slider, a button to spawn additional ragdolls, a rope and a cloth banner to show off the same constraint system, and a slow-motion toggle.
prompts.notes: Watch for: constraints exploding under fast drags; limbs hyper-extending (no angle limits); collision only with the floor, not obstacles; multiple ragdolls tangling into one.

prompts.title: ASCII Roguelike
prompts.prompt: Build a turn-based ASCII roguelike as a single HTML page in vanilla JavaScript — no libraries. Procedurally generate dungeons with connected rooms and corridors across at least 5 descending levels. Include field-of-view with fog of war (explored-but-unseen areas dimmed), monsters with simple chase AI that take turns when you move, melee combat with HP/attack/defense, healing potions and weapon pickups, an inventory, a message log, stairs down, a final goal item, and permadeath with a run summary. Render in a monospace grid with colour.
prompts.notes: Watch for: disconnected rooms (unreachable areas); FOV seeing through walls; monsters moving on the player's turn or not at all; combat math with no feedback in the log.

prompts.prompt: Build the game 2048 as a single HTML page in vanilla JavaScript — no libraries. Tiles must slide with smooth animations and merge correctly (each tile merges at most once per move), with new tiles spawning in random empty cells. Support arrow keys and touch swipes, score plus localStorage best score, a single-use undo per move, a win state at 2048 with the option to continue, and a game-over detection that only triggers when no moves remain. Match the classic tile colour scheme.
prompts.notes: Watch for: double merges in one move (4-4-4-4 becoming 16); moves registered when nothing can slide; animations desynced from the logical grid; game over declared with merges still available.

prompts.title: Isometric City Builder
prompts.prompt: Build a small isometric city builder as a single HTML page in vanilla JavaScript and canvas — no libraries or image assets; draw all isometric tiles in code. On a 20x20 grid the player places roads, houses, shops, parks, and power plants, each with a cost. Houses only grow population if connected to a road and powered; shops generate income from nearby population. Run a simulation tick every few seconds updating money and population shown in a HUD, include bulldoze mode, hover highlighting with valid/invalid placement feedback, and save/load to localStorage.
prompts.notes: Watch for: isometric screen-to-tile picking off by half a tile; depth sorting drawing back tiles over front ones; road connectivity never checked; economy that only goes up.

prompts.title: Fireworks Display
prompts.prompt: Build a fireworks display as a single HTML page in vanilla JavaScript and canvas — no libraries. Rockets launch from the bottom with a trail, arc realistically, and explode into distinct types: peony (sphere), willow (long drooping trails), crackle (secondary mini-explosions), and ring. Click to launch at the cursor, plus an auto-show mode with varied timing and a grand finale button. Render over a night-city silhouette with the display reflected in water at the bottom, and synthesize launch whistles and boom sounds with the Web Audio API (gated behind a first click).
prompts.notes: Watch for: particles without gravity or drag (static starbursts); all explosion types looking identical; reflection just a mirrored copy at full brightness; thousands of particles allocated per frame causing GC stutter.

prompts.title: Chess with AI
prompts.prompt: Build a complete chess game as a single HTML page in vanilla JavaScript — no libraries; draw the pieces with Unicode chess characters or in code. Enforce all rules: legal move generation with check detection, castling, en passant, pawn promotion with a piece picker, stalemate, checkmate, and draw by insufficient material. Include click-or-drag moving with legal-move highlighting, a minimax AI opponent with alpha-beta pruning searching at least 3 plies with adjustable difficulty, algebraic move notation in a scrollable list, board flip, and an undo button.
prompts.notes: Watch for: moves allowed that leave the king in check; castling/en passant missing or wrong; AI taking forever (no pruning) or playing randomly; promotion auto-queening with no choice.

prompts.title: Million Particle Field
prompts.prompt: Build a single HTML page that renders up to 1,000,000 particles at interactive frame rates using WebGL2 in plain JavaScript — no libraries. Use GPU-friendly techniques (instancing or transform feedback; do not update particles one-by-one on the CPU). The mouse acts as an attractor, switching to a repulsor while the button is held. Colour particles by speed, add slight motion blur or trail fading, and include a particle count selector (10k / 100k / 1M), an FPS counter, and a force-strength slider. It should remain above 30fps at 1M particles on a typical discrete GPU.
prompts.notes: Watch for: CPU-side per-particle loops (instant failure at 1M); requiring WebGL2 without a fallback message; attractor force exploding velocities; FPS counter measuring the wrong thing.

prompts.title: VR Controller Playground
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page WebXR playground for the Meta Quest 3 using Three.js. Enter VR with a VRButton, use a local-floor reference space, and render both Touch controllers with XRControllerModelFactory plus laser pointers. The user can point at and grab physics-driven cubes and spheres from a table, throw them with a release velocity that matches the real hand motion, and feel a haptic pulse on grab and on collision. Include a world-space UI panel with buttons and a gravity slider driven by the laser pointer, an FPS/latency readout, and a desktop fallback with an orbit camera and mouse-drag grabbing so the scene can be reviewed without a headset.
prompts.notes: Watch for: three.js addons (VRButton, XRControllerModelFactory) imported without an import map so nothing loads; throw velocity taken from a single frame's delta instead of smoothed controller motion; a grabbed object reparented without preserving its world transform, so it jumps; the UI panel not raycastable; nothing rendered at all outside a VR session.

prompts.title: VR Teleport Gallery
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js WebXR art gallery for the Quest 3 with three locomotion modes the user can switch between: parabolic-arc teleport on the right thumbstick with a landing marker that turns red on invalid surfaces, snap turn on the left thumbstick with a configurable angle, and optional smooth locomotion with a comfort vignette. Lay out several connected rooms with framed pictures, doorways, benches and a skylight, and put the settings panel on the left controller's wrist. Teleport must only accept floor geometry and must move the player rig, not the camera. Include a desktop WASD plus pointer-lock fallback.
prompts.notes: Watch for: teleport moving the camera object instead of the XR rig group; the arc passing through walls and still allowing the teleport; snap turn rotating about the world origin rather than about the user's head position; the vignette drawn as a screen overlay that breaks stereo; no usable controls on desktop.

prompts.title: VR Paint Studio
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js WebXR 3D painting app for the Quest 3. Holding the trigger draws a ribbon stroke that follows the controller, with width driven by trigger pressure and the ribbon oriented to stay readable from the viewer. The off-hand controller carries a wrist palette: colour wheel, brush type (flat ribbon, tube, glowing neon, sparkle particles), width, and undo/redo/clear. Both grips together grab the whole painting to move, rotate and scale it. Include a grid floor for reference, stroke count and triangle budget on screen, and export of the artwork as a downloadable file. Provide a desktop mouse-drawing fallback.
prompts.notes: Watch for: every stroke rebuilding a BufferGeometry each frame and destroying framerate; the ribbon flipping or pinching when the controller rolls; undo clearing everything instead of the last stroke; the palette placed in world space instead of attached to the controller; the export downloading an empty or unopenable file.

prompts.title: Passthrough Room Planner
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page WebXR mixed-reality room planner for the Quest 3's passthrough. Request an immersive-ar session with hit-test and plane-detection as optional features, show a placement reticle on real surfaces, and let the user place, move, rotate and delete furniture (sofa, table, chair, lamp, rug, shelf) chosen from a wrist menu using the controller ray. Items snap to the detected floor and align to walls, cast a soft contact shadow onto the passthrough, and a tape-measure tool reports distances in metres. Persist the layout to localStorage. Degrade gracefully to an opaque VR room, and then to a plain desktop scene, when passthrough is unavailable.
prompts.notes: Watch for: the session requested without optionalFeatures so hit-test and plane-detection silently do nothing; an opaque background or skybox occluding the passthrough feed; objects placed at the reticle's screen position rather than its world pose; no message or fallback when immersive-ar is unsupported; measurements reported in scene units instead of metres.

prompts.title: Hand-Tracking Instrument
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js WebXR musical instrument for the Quest 3 played entirely with hand tracking — no controllers. Request the hand-tracking feature, render both hands from their XRHand joint poses each frame, and float a curved arc of pads within arm's reach that light up and sound when a fingertip crosses into them. Synthesise everything with the Web Audio API (no audio files) using per-note envelopes, a pinch on the left hand to change voice, and pinch-and-drag to reposition the whole instrument. Show a clear indicator when tracking is lost and recover cleanly. Provide a mouse-clickable desktop fallback.
prompts.notes: Watch for: joint poses read once at session start instead of from each XRFrame; a note retriggering every frame while the finger stays inside a pad; the AudioContext never resumed after a user gesture so there is silence; no handling of hands dropping out of tracking; pinch detected on a bare distance threshold with no hysteresis, so it chatters.

prompts.title: VR Archery Range
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js WebXR archery range for the Quest 3. One controller grips the bow and the other grabs the string; draw strength comes from the world-space distance between the two controllers, the bow and string deform visibly as it is drawn, and releasing the trigger looses an arrow with matching speed, a gravity arc and a haptic thump. Targets stand at varying distances with scoring rings, some sliding side to side, and arrows stick where they land. Include a timed round, per-shot score with ring detection, a wind indicator, and a localStorage high-score table. Provide a desktop mouse aim-and-charge fallback.
prompts.notes: Watch for: draw distance measured in local rather than world space so it changes as the player turns; arrows spawning behind or inside the bow mesh; no gravity, making every shot trivial; hit scoring against a bounding box so the rings are meaningless; haptics called on an input source that has no gamepad, throwing an error.

prompts.title: Rhythm Saber Arena
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js WebXR rhythm game for the Quest 3 in the saber-slicing style. Two glowing blades attached to the controllers cut blocks flying toward the player on a beat grid; each block carries a required colour and slice direction, and a cut only counts when the correct saber crosses it moving roughly the right way and above a minimum speed — otherwise the block breaks the combo. Generate the track procedurally with the Web Audio API and derive the chart from the audio clock, with no audio files. Include combo and score, obstacle walls to duck or lean around, haptics on a clean cut, and a desktop keyboard fallback for reviewing the chart.
prompts.notes: Watch for: hits scored on proximity alone, ignoring slice direction and speed; saber motion sampled once per frame with no swept test, so fast swings tunnel straight through blocks; the chart drifting because timing uses requestAnimationFrame time instead of AudioContext.currentTime; a fresh mesh and material allocated per block instead of pooling.

prompts.title: VR Data Observatory
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js WebXR data explorer for the Quest 3. Embed a dataset of at least 200 rows with four numeric columns and one category, and render it as a 3D scatter plot in a room-scale volume with labelled, scaled axes alongside a linked bar-chart panel. Pointing a controller ray at a point shows a floating tooltip that faces the head; the trigger selects a category and highlights it across both views. One grip moves the plot, both grips together scale and rotate it around the midpoint between the hands. A wrist menu switches between scatter, bars and parallel coordinates. Include a desktop orbit-control fallback.
prompts.notes: Watch for: two-handed scaling computed from the current controller distance with no stored reference, so the plot jumps the instant it is grabbed; a canvas-texture label allocated per data point, collapsing framerate; tooltips that do not billboard toward the head; axes drawn without ticks or units; raycast picking that silently fails against instanced geometry.

prompts.title: VR Cockpit Space Flight
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js WebXR seated space-flight sim for the Quest 3. The player sits in a cockpit whose throttle lever and flight stick are physical objects the controllers grab: the stick's constrained tilt drives pitch, yaw and roll, the throttle's travel along its rail drives speed, and both move mechanically with detents and resistance. Fly through an asteroid field with a starfield, a radar dish, shield and hull gauges on real cockpit panels, rings to fly through, and a docking approach with alignment cues. Keep the cockpit rigidly fixed to the player's reference space, offer a comfort-vignette toggle and a recentre button, and provide a desktop keyboard-and-mouse fallback.
prompts.notes: Watch for: the cockpit drifting relative to the head so the whole scene swims and induces sickness; a grabbed lever following the controller freely instead of being projected onto its axis and clamped; pitch/yaw/roll applied as world-space Euler angles, producing gimbal artefacts; collision checks looping over every asteroid every frame; no way to recentre the seated view.

prompts.title: VR Escape Room
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js WebXR escape room for the Quest 3 built on physical interaction rather than menus. A sealed study contains a combination dial turned by twisting a grabbed controller, a lever to pull, drawers and a door that open only by grabbing and dragging along their real axis, a key that must be carried to a lock, a UV torch that reveals hidden markings on the walls, and a note whose code opens the safe. The puzzles chain so the room must be solved in order. Include teleport locomotion, grab-anywhere handling with haptics, an in-world hint plaque, a reset button, and a desktop click-to-interact fallback.
prompts.notes: Watch for: interactions reduced to clicking floating buttons instead of constrained physical motion; the dial reading absolute controller rotation so it snaps to a new value the moment it is grabbed; drawers and doors sliding off their rails or passing through the furniture; the chain solvable out of order or the safe openable without the code; no way to reset the room after a mistake.

prompts.title: Hold-the-Solar-System
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page Three.js WebXR orrery for the Quest 3 that the player can hold and grow. It begins as a table-top model with correct relative orbital periods and inclinations; grabbing it with both grips and pulling the hands apart scales it continuously from a model in the palm to a system the player stands inside, with the sun's light falloff, planet sizes and orbit lines all staying believable across the range. Pointing at a planet raises an info card that faces the head, the trigger flies the view smoothly to it, and a wrist dial scrubs time forward and backward from a single time value. Include a desktop orbit-control fallback.
prompts.notes: Watch for: scale applied to the camera rig instead of the model, which breaks the floor height and the stereo separation; two-handed scaling with no stored initial hand distance so the model snaps on grab; orbital periods invented rather than proportional to the real ones; info cards clipping inside planets; time scrubbing accumulating drift instead of being derived from one clock value.

prompts.title: Raw WebXR, No Libraries
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page WebXR experience for the Quest 3 using raw WebGL2 and the WebXR Device API only — no Three.js and no libraries of any kind. Request an immersive-vr session with a local-floor reference space, render every view of each XRFrame from the XRWebGLLayer's viewports, and draw a grid floor plus a field of lit, spinning cubes with your own GLSL shaders and your own matrix maths. Read both controllers from their grip and target-ray spaces, draw a ray from each, and let the trigger recolour whichever cube it points at. Include an Enter VR button, a clear message when WebXR is unsupported, and a non-XR desktop preview of the same scene with a mouse-orbit camera.
prompts.notes: Watch for: the scene drawn once per frame instead of once per view, giving a mono or one-eyed image; the XRWebGLLayer framebuffer never bound, so the headset shows black; window.requestAnimationFrame used instead of the session's own frame loop; view and projection matrices multiplied in the wrong order; no path at all when navigator.xr is missing.

prompts.title: SimCity-Style City Simulator
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page city-building simulator in the spirit of the original SimCity, using HTML5 Canvas and vanilla JavaScript with no external assets. The map is a 64×64 tile grid with terrain (land, water, trees). The player lays roads, power lines and power plants, and zones Residential, Commercial and Industrial land; zones only grow when they are connected to a road and powered. Model RCI demand as three meters that respond to the balance of jobs and population, land value driven by pollution, crime and proximity to parks, and police/fire station coverage radii. Run a monthly budget with tax rate sliders, maintenance costs and a running treasury. Include overlay views (power, pollution, land value, crime, traffic density), pause/1×/3× speed controls, a date and population readout, random disasters (fire that spreads, tornado), and save/load to localStorage.
prompts.notes: Watch for: zones that grow without road or power connectivity; power flood-fill recomputed every frame instead of on change so large cities crawl; RCI demand that never responds to the jobs/population balance; overlays that are just recolored tiles with no underlying field; a budget that can go infinitely negative with no consequence.

prompts.title: Gaia Planet Simulator
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page planetary simulator in the spirit of SimEarth, using Canvas and vanilla JavaScript. Show a wrap-around equirectangular world map (e.g. 128×64 cells) where each cell tracks elevation, temperature, rainfall and biome (ocean, ice, desert, grassland, forest, jungle, tundra). Simulate a simple energy balance: solar input by latitude, albedo from ice and cloud, greenhouse strength from atmospheric CO₂, and heat diffusion between neighbouring cells, so an ice-albedo feedback can tip the planet into a snowball or runaway greenhouse. Life spreads and evolves through eras (single-celled → plants → animals → intelligence) based on habitability. Give the player god-controls: raise/lower terrain, seed life, inject or scrub CO₂, adjust solar output, trigger volcanoes and meteor strikes. Include map-layer toggles, global time-series charts (mean temperature, CO₂, ice cover, biomass) and a speed slider covering millions of years per second.
prompts.notes: Watch for: a temperature field with no latitude gradient; missing ice-albedo feedback so nothing ever tips; biomes assigned from temperature alone ignoring rainfall; the map not wrapping east–west during diffusion; charts that grow unbounded arrays until the tab slows.

prompts.title: London Bus Simulator
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page London bus driving simulator with Three.js (import via an import map). The player drives a red double-decker Routemaster built from primitives, on the left-hand side of the road, through a procedurally generated London street grid with terraced buildings, zebra crossings, traffic lights, black cabs and other AI traffic that obeys signals. The route has numbered bus stops with shelters; the player must pull into the stop, open the doors, and wait while waiting passengers board and alighting passengers leave, with boarding time proportional to headcount. Model bus physics with a long wheelbase, weight-dependent acceleration and braking, and a rear that swings wide on tight corners. Score punctuality against a timetable, passenger comfort (penalise harsh braking and cornering g-force), and fines for running red lights or hitting kerbs. Include chase, cab and top-deck cameras, a HUD with speedometer, next stop, schedule delta and passenger count, plus a minimap.
prompts.notes: Watch for: the bus driving on the right; a turning model that pivots on its centre instead of rear-axle steering geometry; AI traffic that drives through the bus or ignores lights; passengers who teleport instead of walking to the doors; no way to fail the timetable.

prompts.title: Fed Chair: Monetary Policy Simulator
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page economic simulator where the player is the chair of the Federal Reserve, using vanilla JavaScript and Canvas or SVG charts. Each turn is one FOMC meeting (eight per year). The player sets the federal funds rate in 25bp steps, chooses a balance-sheet policy (QE, hold, QT) and picks a forward-guidance statement from a list of hawkish/neutral/dovish options. Under the hood, run a small New-Keynesian-style model: an IS curve linking real rates to the output gap with a lag, an expectations-augmented Phillips curve, inflation expectations that de-anchor if the Fed loses credibility, an unemployment rate via Okun's law, bond yields and a stock index that react to surprises versus market expectations. Throw random shocks (oil spike, banking panic, pandemic, productivity boom) with headline news tickers. Show a Taylor-rule benchmark for comparison, dashboard charts of inflation, unemployment, GDP growth, rates and credibility, and end-of-term grading on the dual mandate. Include a congressional testimony event with multiple-choice answers that affect credibility.
prompts.notes: Watch for: policy that affects inflation instantly with no transmission lag; markets reacting to the rate level rather than the surprise versus expectations; expectations that never de-anchor so credibility is decorative; a Taylor rule computed with the wrong sign on the output gap; shocks with no persistence.

prompts.title: Stock Market Trading Simulator
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page stock market trading simulator in vanilla JavaScript with Canvas charts. Simulate eight fictional tickers whose prices follow geometric Brownian motion with sector correlations, volatility clustering and occasional jump events tied to generated news headlines (earnings beats, scandals, sector rallies). Show a live candlestick chart with selectable timeframes, volume bars and moving-average/RSI overlays, plus a Level-2 order book and time-and-sales tape driven by simulated market participants. The player starts with $100,000 and can place market, limit and stop orders, go long or short, and use optional 2× margin with margin calls. Track positions, average cost, realised and unrealised P&L, fees, and an equity curve versus an index of all eight stocks. Include speed controls (pause, 1 tick/s up to 100×), a trading-day clock with open/close auctions, and a final performance report with Sharpe ratio and max drawdown.
prompts.notes: Watch for: prices that can go negative (arithmetic rather than geometric motion); limit orders filling at the limit price when the market gapped through it; short P&L with the wrong sign; candles built from a single tick; a Sharpe ratio that is not annualised or ignores the risk-free rate.

prompts.title: School Headteacher Simulator
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page school management simulator where the player is the headteacher, using Canvas and vanilla JavaScript. Show a top-down school floor plan with classrooms, a hall, playground, canteen and staff room, where individual students and teachers walk between rooms following the bell timetable. Each student has attributes (ability, motivation, wellbeing, attendance, friendship group) and each teacher has subject, skill, energy and morale. The player hires and fires staff within a budget, builds the weekly timetable, sets class sizes, spends on facilities (library, science lab, sports hall), and chooses policies (homework load, uniform strictness, after-school clubs, anti-bullying) that trade off grades against wellbeing and teacher burnout. Random events include illness outbreaks, a teacher resigning, a parent complaint, and a surprise inspection that grades the school on attainment, behaviour and leadership. Run the simulation through terms and years with exam results, league-table position and parent applications driving next year's intake and funding.
prompts.notes: Watch for: students who never actually move between rooms on the bell; a timetable that allows a teacher in two rooms at once; policies that only change a number with no emergent effect on individuals; an inspection that ignores the metrics being simulated; no pressure from the budget.

prompts.title: Epidemic Outbreak Simulator
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page epidemic simulator with Canvas that runs an agent-based SEIR model side by side with the equivalent compartmental differential-equation model. Hundreds of agents move between homes, workplaces, schools and shops across a small town; infection probability depends on proximity, time exposed, and the pathogen's transmissibility. Expose sliders for R₀, incubation and infectious periods, asymptomatic fraction and fatality rate, and interventions: masks, social distancing, school closures, testing and isolation, contact tracing and vaccination rollout with a daily capacity. Show a live stacked area chart of S/E/I/R/D, an effective-R readout, hospital occupancy against a capacity line, and a map heat layer of infections. Include preset scenarios (seasonal flu, measles, novel pandemic) and a cost panel showing the economic damage of each intervention.
prompts.notes: Watch for: agents that infect at any distance; R₀ slider not actually calibrating the transmission rate; the ODE model and agent model using different parameter meanings so they never agree; interventions toggled with no delay or compliance; chart arrays growing without limit.

prompts.title: Predator-Prey Evolution Simulator
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page ecosystem simulator with Canvas where grass, rabbits and foxes live on a 2D landscape. Grass regrows on a per-tile timer; rabbits eat grass, foxes hunt rabbits, and every creature has energy, age and a genome of heritable traits (speed, vision range, size, reproduction threshold) that mutate slightly on birth, with speed and size costing energy. Creatures steer using simple behaviours: seek food, flee predators, find mates, wander. Show population curves that should oscillate like a Lotka–Volterra system, histograms of each trait over time so the player can watch natural selection, and a click-to-inspect panel for any creature with its lineage. Provide controls to adjust mutation rate, food growth and starting populations, spawn disasters (drought, disease), and speed up time to thousands of ticks per second without rendering.
prompts.notes: Watch for: populations that crash to zero within seconds because energy costs aren't balanced; traits that mutate but give no fitness advantage or cost; neighbour searches that are O(n²) with no spatial hash; fast-forward still rendering every tick; histograms that never update.

prompts.title: Ant Colony Simulator
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page ant colony simulator with Canvas and vanilla JavaScript. Thousands of ants leave a nest to forage, laying 'to-home' and 'to-food' pheromone trails on a grid that evaporates and diffuses over time; ants sense pheromone with three forward sensors and steer toward the strongest, producing emergent shortest-path trails. The player can paint food sources, walls and water, and drag the nest. Include caste roles (workers, soldiers), a colony food store that funds new ant spawning, a rival colony that competes for food and fights on contact, and toggles to visualise each pheromone map as a coloured overlay. Expose sliders for evaporation rate, diffusion, sensor angle and ant count, and show live stats for population and food collected per minute.
prompts.notes: Watch for: ants that know where food is instead of sensing pheromones; trails that never evaporate so every path saturates; per-ant object allocations each frame killing performance; ants walking through walls; no emergent path shortening when two routes exist.

prompts.title: Traffic Flow Simulator
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page traffic simulator with Canvas that uses the Intelligent Driver Model for car-following and MOBIL for lane changes. Provide three scenarios: a single-lane ring road that demonstrates phantom traffic jams (let the user tap a car to brake briefly and watch the stop-and-go wave travel backwards), a multi-lane motorway with an on-ramp merge and a lane closure, and a four-way junction with configurable traffic-light phase timings versus a roundabout. Expose sliders for inflow rate, desired speed, safe time headway, politeness factor and the fraction of trucks. Show a time-space diagram of vehicle positions, a live flow/density fundamental diagram, and throughput and average delay stats so the player can find the best light timings.
prompts.notes: Watch for: cars that pass through each other at high density; IDM acceleration going to infinity when the gap reaches zero; lane changes that ignore the vehicle behind in the target lane; the ring-road jam not forming because every car is identical and perfectly smooth; a time-space diagram drawn with no time axis history.

prompts.title: Air Traffic Control Simulator
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page air traffic control simulator with a green-on-black radar scope drawn on Canvas, including a rotating sweep, range rings, runways, waypoints and a fading history trail of each aircraft's previous returns. Aircraft enter from the edges with callsigns, type, altitude and destination (land at one of two runways or exit via a named fix). The player selects an aircraft and issues heading, altitude and speed instructions or a clear-to-land command; aircraft turn at a realistic rate, climb and descend gradually, and pilots read back instructions in a text log. Enforce separation minimums (3 nm lateral / 1000 ft vertical) with conflict alerts, fuel limits and go-arounds for bad approaches. Increase traffic density over time, show a score for landed and handed-off flights, and end the shift on a loss of separation.
prompts.notes: Watch for: aircraft that snap instantly to new headings or altitudes; turns always going the same direction instead of the shortest way; separation checked only laterally; landing accepted from any heading or altitude; a sweep that redraws every aircraft continuously instead of on each pass.

prompts.title: Orbital Rocket Launch Simulator
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page rocket launch and orbital mechanics simulator on Canvas. The player designs a rocket by stacking stages (each with engine thrust, specific impulse, fuel mass and dry mass) and sees the computed delta-v per stage from the Tsiolkovsky equation. Launch from a planet with atmospheric drag that thins with altitude and a gravity turn controlled by the player's pitch. Integrate the trajectory with a stable integrator (velocity Verlet or RK4) and draw the predicted conic orbit with apoapsis/periapsis markers. Support staging, throttle, time warp (disabled inside the atmosphere), prograde/retrograde burns, and a moon that the player can attempt to reach using a transfer burn with sphere-of-influence switching. Show a HUD with altitude, velocity, dynamic pressure, remaining delta-v and a navball-style heading indicator, plus mission goals (reach orbit, circularise, lunar flyby).
prompts.notes: Watch for: Euler integration that makes stable orbits spiral out; delta-v shown that ignores staging; time warp that breaks the physics at high multipliers; the predicted orbit not matching the actual path; drag applied in vacuum or with the wrong sign.

prompts.title: Power Grid Operator Simulator
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page electricity grid control-room simulator in vanilla JavaScript. Demand follows a realistic 24-hour curve with weather and a TV-pickup surge; supply comes from dispatchable plants with ramp rates and start-up times (nuclear, coal, gas CCGT, gas peakers, hydro), variable wind and solar driven by a weather forecast that can be wrong, and grid batteries. The player commits and dispatches units ahead of time and in real time. Model system frequency around 50 Hz using inertia: any mismatch between supply and demand moves frequency, low inertia from renewables makes it swing faster, and falling below thresholds triggers automatic load shedding and eventually a blackout. Track cost per MWh, CO₂ emissions and reliability, and display a stacked generation chart, frequency trace and a map of plants and substations. Include scenario days (winter peak, windless week, heatwave, plant trip).
prompts.notes: Watch for: frequency that does not depend on system inertia; plants that ramp from zero to full instantly; solar producing at night; a stacked chart that doesn't sum to demand; no penalty for over-generation.

prompts.title: Emergency Department Simulator
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page hospital emergency department simulator with Canvas. Patients arrive by walk-in and ambulance following a time-of-day Poisson arrival rate, are triaged into five acuity levels, and flow through waiting room, cubicles, resus bays, imaging, and either discharge or admission to a ward that has limited beds (bed-blocking backs up the department). The player manages a shift roster of doctors and nurses with fatigue, opens escalation areas, and diverts ambulances at a cost. Show animated patients moving between zones, live metrics for 4-hour target compliance, median wait by acuity, patients leaving without being seen and ambulance handover delays, plus a queue-length chart. Include a major-incident event and let the player compare a staffing plan across a simulated week with a fixed random seed.
prompts.notes: Watch for: arrivals at a constant rate rather than Poisson with a daily pattern; acuity ignored so critical patients wait behind minor injuries; beds that free instantly with no ward blocking; no seeded RNG so plans can't be compared fairly; staff fatigue that has no effect.

prompts.title: Evolving Walkers Simulator
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page evolution simulator where creatures made of nodes and muscles (springs that contract rhythmically) learn to walk to the right across a 2D terrain. Implement the soft-body physics with a fixed timestep: gravity, spring forces, ground friction and collision. Each generation of 100 creatures is simulated for 15 seconds headlessly (optionally in a Web Worker) and scored by distance travelled; the best reproduce with mutation of node positions, muscle lengths, strengths and timing, plus occasional structural mutations that add or remove nodes and muscles. Show the current champion replaying, a fitness-over-generations chart with best/median/worst, a species diversity bar, and a gallery of ancestors. Provide buttons to run 1, 10 or 100 generations quickly and to save/load a population.
prompts.notes: Watch for: physics tied to frame rate so results change between runs; creatures that exploit the simulation by exploding upward; mutations that break connectivity leaving floating nodes; fitness measured from the start node rather than the centre of mass; the UI freezing while generations run.

prompts.title: Seasonal Farm Simulator
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page farm management simulator on Canvas with a top-down tiled farm. Crops (wheat, potatoes, rapeseed, barley) each have a planting window, growth stages drawn per tile, water and nitrogen needs, and yields affected by soil quality that depletes and recovers with crop rotation, fallow and fertiliser. Weather is generated daily per season with rain, frost and drought, and the player can irrigate at a cost. Include livestock (sheep, cows) that need grazing land and feed, equipment purchases that speed up field work, hired labour, and a commodity market whose prices move with a supply/demand model and seasonal patterns so the player can store and sell at the right time. Show a calendar, cash-flow chart, field soil-health overlay and an end-of-year accounts statement.
prompts.notes: Watch for: crops that grow identically regardless of weather or soil; no depletion so monoculture has no downside; a market with purely random prices; seasons that don't constrain planting; days that pass with no field-work capacity limit.

prompts.title: Island Nation Economy Simulator
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page agent-based economy simulator for a small island nation in vanilla JavaScript. Hundreds of households and firms interact: households supply labour, consume goods and save; firms hire, set prices and wages based on inventory and demand, invest, and go bankrupt; a bank makes loans at an interest rate and creates money in the process. The player is the finance minister and sets income tax, corporation tax, government spending, a minimum wage and import tariffs, and can trade with the outside world at a floating exchange rate. Show emergent macro statistics (GDP, unemployment, inflation, inequality via a Gini coefficient and Lorenz curve, government debt) with live charts, and a firm-level scatter of size versus profitability. Include a boom-bust credit cycle that can emerge naturally and preset shocks (tourism collapse, commodity boom).
prompts.notes: Watch for: money appearing or disappearing with no accounting (stock-flow inconsistency); firms setting prices randomly instead of from inventory signals; a Gini coefficient computed on an unsorted list; unemployment that can go negative; policy sliders that change aggregates directly instead of agent behaviour.

prompts.title: Weather Systems Simulator
prompts.prompt: Build a single-page weather simulator on Canvas over a 2D map of a coastline with mountains. Run a simple atmospheric model on a grid: pressure, temperature, humidity and wind velocity, with advection, a Coriolis effect that makes wind circulate around lows and highs, sea breezes from land–sea heating contrast through the day, orographic lift that forces rain on windward slopes and a rain shadow behind, and cloud formation when air cools past its dew point. The player can place high and low pressure centres, adjust sea temperature and time of year, and watch fronts and storms develop. Render wind as animated streamlines or particles, clouds with opacity from liquid water, rain as a precipitation layer, and isobars as contours. Include a forecast panel for a clicked town showing temperature, wind and rain for the next 48 simulated hours.
prompts.notes: Watch for: wind blowing straight from high to low pressure with no Coriolis deflection; no rain shadow behind mountains; numerical blow-up from advection with too large a timestep; isobars drawn as noise rather than contours of the actual field; day–night heating missing so sea breezes never form.
